policy.trigger: When an assistant/operator-authored production MCP change causes a severe recurring regression, or the user explicitly reports the previously working MCP regressed after our change and requests restoration, restore the last known-working production behavior/topology before speculative fixes.
required_order: If the user explicitly asks for platform-reroute/security analysis or incident tracking, log any user-observed reroute with report/event-time semantics before further MCP/edge mutation; otherwise treat platform security events as external and do not persist them.
Preserve the current runtime, dist, serving identity, and rollback evidence.
Use the production change gate, exact Busy scope, independent rollback, off-path proof, and drain active child processes before cutover.
Restore the frozen production behavior and topology; a source SHA alone is not sufficient when topology differs. Use only the minimal compatibility required by the proven replacement mechanism.
Do not stack unrelated logging, diagnostics, guards, or speculative fixes onto the regressed serving runtime before restoration.
After restoration, verify public route, Host handling, OAuth/tool contract, canonical port, and candidate drain.

If the client-visible symptom persists after restoration while bounded transport evidence shows no MCP request in flight at the symptom time, classify that event as above-MCP/platform evidence and stop MCP/edge mutation unless new MCP-local evidence appears.
policy.preservation_rule: Restoration must preserve unique work and active child processes; do not kill foreign work to accelerate recovery.
policy.authorization_rule: Routine reversible shared-production restoration or serving advance that is already the established scoped objective is authorized by go/continue once the existing production-change safety gates pass; do not ask for redundant per-cutover approval. Separate explicit user authorization remains required only for scope-widening, destructive overwrite of user/foreign state, scheduler/fleet mutation, credential/permission changes, or shared production topology/control-plane redesign.
recovery_invariants: During an active MCP incident, keep the selected recovery target fixed unless new evidence positively disqualifies it; do not search for or promote a 'better' target mid-recovery.

Before any serving-path mutation, including stopping, killing, restarting, retargeting, disabling, or deleting an MCP listener/launcher/task/process tree, reconcile the selected deployment artifact, the live backend artifact/generation, the live transport/topology, the exact active caller/session route from live transport evidence, and an independent rollback/control route. Instance names, task names, port labels, or strings such as 'test'/'debug' are never evidence that a route is disposable.
If the live backend artifact already matches the selected recovery artifact and only topology differs, restore only the topology; do not restart or replace the backend.

MCP serving repair must not depend solely on the same MCP request path being repaired. If the target is used by the active caller/session, or its route role is unresolved, mutation is blocked until an independently verified control/rollback route exists; preserve the target instead of inferring safety from a local-looking name or port.
Automatic Caddy routing is WireGuard 10.203.0.2:3011; SSH 3101-3104 lanes are explicit recovery only. A reverse-SSH primary is topology drift, not a new recovery target.
A 502 that leaves no Node/backend request row proves only that the request did not reach the Node app; exclude Caddy/VPS/tunnel/listener failure before classifying it as above-MCP/platform.

conditions.message: Canonical/public health and host/OAuth acceptance passed for this deployment generation.
The three process tools are live with the intended annotations and bounded live validation passed.

Observed direct-tool-block evidence fell from 3 known occurrences across 17,141 pre-refresh process calls (0.175019 per 1,000) to 0 across 7,105 post-refresh calls, but the post zero-event one-sided 95% Poisson upper bound is about 0.422 per 1,000 and the equal-exposure control is also sparse. The underlying reduction is therefore not statistically established; broader user-visible/above-MCP reroutes persist.

The completed 48-hour post-refresh acceptance window contains two preserved exact user-visible adverse occurrence windows, and a fresh same-operation OpenAI pre-dispatch safety block recurred during mature evaluation while this generation was live. The broader platform-side safety/routing class is not eliminated; this does not attribute causality to the backend generation.

The configured observation threshold elapsed and real-use acceptance failed: the corrected analyzer reports RECURRENCE_OBSERVED from two exact user-visible occurrence windows across the 48-hour campaign, and a fresh pre-dispatch safety block also recurred. Long-run acceptable stability is therefore false; selected recovery-target identity remains unchanged.

LongRunStable.rule: Set LongRunStable to True or False from real-use evidence after the observation window; do not rename or promote the deployment.

Broader user-visible/above-MCP reroutes persist, so no causal or elimination claim is supported.

notes: Recovery-target selection and observed conditions are independent facts. Never infer whole-system health from the selected recovery target.
Conditions use True/False/Unknown and are tied to the observed deployment generation; update only the condition supported by new evidence.
Do not recreate any promotion label that combines recovery-target selection with health. LongRunStable can be Unknown while the same deployment remains the preferred recovery target.

Current operational truth is SecurityReroutesReduced=Unknown and SecurityReroutesEliminated=False: a lower observed direct-block count is real, but sparse normalized evidence does not yet establish a reduced underlying rate.
Incident recovery invariant: the selected recovery target remains fixed during an outage unless positive evidence disqualifies it; rollback-target search is not a debugging loop.
Before any MCP serving mutation, compare selected artifact, live backend artifact/generation, live Caddy transport, and independent control route. Restore only the proven divergent component.
LongRunStable=False records mature acceptance failure from user-visible/platform-side recurrence; it does not change or disqualify the selected recovery target and does not assign backend causality.
